p1_readers_not_connected.verdict: ACCEPTED IN FULL. The readers existed and nothing called them; the PLAN sentence describing selection through them described an intended change absent from those bytes.

connected.StageComposition.end: `deployment.publication` -> `publication_for(assignment['participant'])`. Under several producers `_PerJobPublication` refuses on every call, so a second Job could not reach its ending at all. The producer is the ending attempt's OWN assignment participant, which is the one session `Authority.publish` can act for.
connected.Integration.required_tests: SELECTS THE PRODUCING ATTEMPT'S WORKER, by the Job binding's own `source_worker_id`, and no longer refuses for having more than one implementation worker. It is NOT the integration worker allocated for the current stage, which is what the review named.
connected.Integration.account: the first integration-role worker -> `worker_for(stage)`, and the global Work/target -> `works_for`/`target_for` of this stage's Job
connected.factory session scope: `_work_scope(job_work_id)` -> `_bound_scope`, which reads EVERY bound Work's own effective scope and REFUSES a disagreement (policy/denied) rather than inventing a grant reaching both. `_write_receipt` derives a receipt's scope from the proposal's own Work, so one session set minted for the first Job's Work would have written the second Job's receipts under the wrong grant. Minting a session set per Work is the honest answer to Works whose grants genuinely differ and is a larger cut than this one; the disagreement is named here instead of widened.

p1_readers_not_connected.doubles_and_one_job_preserved: `_bound_id(deployment, stage, job)` is the single rule: read-only observation and the accepted integration cases reach these consumers through a deployment DOUBLE that holds the configuration and not this composition's readers, and through stages carrying no Job. Both get exactly the answer they were accepted with. `/1` is unchanged.

p1_admission_and_work_mismatch.where_it_now_happens: `_job_eligibility`, supplied to the EXISTING `PooledManagerOperations(..., independence=)` seam. `_allocation` calls it with the stage BEFORE `reserve`, so an unbound Job and an incoherent one are both refused ahead of any allocation, offer or setup -- the accepted before-wrong-setup boundary.

p1_admission_and_work_mismatch.single_worker_untouched: its validation is not weakened and keeps every operand it always had. What changed is that assembly stops handing it an incoherent one.

p1_declared_gap_withdrawn.verdict: MY CLAIM WAS UNSUPPORTED AND I WITHDRAW IT. I said two Works necessarily required per-Job worker eligibility in the scheduler or a worker whose manifest is not Work-bound. The seam was already there and public.
p1_declared_gap_withdrawn.how: `_job_eligibility` returns `{'worker_ids': [...]}` excluding every implementation worker that is not this Job's bound producer, so a role-compatible but JOB-incompatible worker is not reservable. `reserve` combines these with the scheduler's own review independence, affinity and principal capacity rules rather than replacing them; selection, affinity and hard independence stay with their current owner. No scheduler or provider edit.
